messages.subject: Point transect and duration
parts:
Hello

For a DS study, we defined the next protocol : data measures at each location point are made on two different time period : one of a 5 min basis, the other on an by adding 5 minutes to the first one. Therefore, for each point, we obtain two results, for a 5 and 10 minutes time period.

DS software gives us results which are different (number of birds and density) according to the duration (see joined file).

Which test(s) can we use to compare the obtained values ?

 

Two teams have been defined for this study : one took notes on paper and the other entered their notes directly on a smartphone application (the same points have been covered by the two teams).

The objective is to compare the two note taking methods. In DS software, do we have to compare the two methods (paper and smartphone) with the same function and same parameters for the two analysis or should we privilegiate the lowest AIC in each analysis ?


Thanks in advance,

Best regards,

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Point transect and duration
parts:
Giles

There are several challenges associated with the comparison you desire.  First, the two density estimates are not independent--data from first five minutes are in both estimates.  That makes a clean comparison difficult.

Also recall that animal movement induces bias in density estimates (see Section 10.1.2 of Buckland et al. (2015)).  If animals move (which they do), waiting long enough animals will come past the observer.  The longer the sampling duration the higher the density estimate.  This is the case in your data for 24 of the 28 species.

Finally, note the precision in most density estimates produces are large relative to the differences observed.  I provide a bit of R code looking at your spreadsheet results.  It produces the magnitude of the density estimates relative to the standard error of the 10minute estimate.  As a rule of thumb, if these values exceed 1.96, you might suggest the difference is statistically meaningful.  Five species (COLPAL, CUCCAN, LUSMEG, TURMER, TURPHI) exceed that threshold.

library(readxl)
fname <- "BILAN 2019 comparaison entre points de 5 et 10 mn.xls"
fdir <- "C:\\Users\\erexs\\Documents\\My Distance Projects"
fullname <- paste(fdir, fname, sep="\\")
thedata <- read_excel(fullname)
hidden <- c(2,3,5,6,8,10,30,32,34) - 1
data <- thedata[-hidden,]

data$DSE <- data$DCV * data$`D estim km2` / 100
data$absdiff <- c(NA,diff(data$`D estim km2`))
diff.serr <- data$absdiff / data$DSE
result <- data.frame(species=unique(data$Espèce),
                   diffSE=round(diff.serr[seq.int(2,length(diff.serr),2)],4))
